graft

Reviewed project memory for the ellmer ecosystem

Give your next agent
the knowledge your team reviewed.

Save findings, metric definitions, and reports with the exact evidence behind them. Record human review and corrections, then let ellmer, shinychat, deputy, or MCP clients recall only what is currently accepted.

Build a project memory assistant See how graft fits the ellmer ecosystem

Why reviewed memory?

Language models start every session from scratch. Conversations live in a chat window; search indexes return whatever matches a query—even drafts, superseded definitions, or withdrawn results.

Suppose your team agrees that an “active customer” has a paid account and used the product in the past 30 days. With graft, your app saves that definition alongside its source, records your review, and exposes a read-only tool to future chats. When the window changes to 60 days, you review the correction while keeping the original evidence and decision history intact.

  1. Save with evidence
  1. Review explicitly
  1. Recall safely
Store text, JSON, reports, or figures with exact references to their inputs. Record who accepted or withdrew a selection—never from an unreviewed model write. Hand graft_tool() to ellmer, shinychat, deputy, or mcptools so agents read only current approved memory.

Try the project notebook app

The package includes a runnable Shiny app pairing a reviewable notebook with a shinychat conversation. By default it runs locally with real graft storage and scripted replies—no API key required.

pak::pak(c("JamesHWade/graft", "ellmer", "shinychat", "shiny", "bslib"))
Sys.setenv(GRAFT_DEMO_STORE = file.path(getwd(), "project-memory"))
shiny::runApp(system.file("examples", "project-memory", package = "graft"))
  1. Review and save the proposed definition and source.
  2. Ask “How do we count an active customer?”
  3. Start a New conversation and ask again—the reviewed definition persists.
  4. Update the definition to 60 days, review the correction, and ask in a fresh chat to verify the updated answer while keeping history intact.

Set OPENAI_API_KEY and Sys.setenv(GRAFT_DEMO_LIVE = "true") to switch to a live ellmer agent. See the getting-started guide for the step-by-step code, deputy runtime integration, and mcptools setup.

Where graft fits in the ellmer ecosystem

graft stays small and composes cleanly with Posit’s ellmerverse and the wider ellmerverse+ stack:

Package Role How it pairs with graft
ellmer & shinychat Model calls, tools, and chat UI Register graft_tool() so chats consult reviewed memory with rich tool cards
ragnar Similarity search (RAG) over documents ragnar finds, graft verifies: use ragnar to locate candidates, then recall only current accepted revisions through graft
commons & data-dict Trusted data analysis & dictionary contracts Commons runs live analyses; graft retains reviewed reports, conclusions, and pinned shared vocabularies across sessions
deputy Governed agent runtime & TrustedResults Run graft_tool() in read-only/plan modes and capture agent drafts via TrustedResults() for human review
mcptools Model Context Protocol servers Serve graft_tool() to Claude Code, Positron, or Posit Assistant
vitals & scans LLM evals & trajectory analysis Evaluate memory recall with vitals and inspect completed agent runs and promotion candidates with scans

Read Graft in the ellmer ecosystem for the full ownership map.

Quick start in R 

library(graft)

store <- graft_store("analysis-memory", create = TRUE)

source <- graft_save(store, "Handbook: use a 30-day activity window.", "handbook")
note <- graft_save(
  store,
  "An active customer has a paid account and activity in the past 30 days.",
  id = "metric:active-customer",
  dependencies = source
)

decision <- graft_accept(
  store,
  note,
  stream = "metric:active-customer",
  expected = NULL,
  key = "review-1",
  actor = "analyst",
  reason = "Matches the metrics handbook",
  purpose = "project-assistance"
)

# Later session or fresh process
recalled <- graft_recall(
  graft_store("analysis-memory"),
  stream = "metric:active-customer",
  purpose = "project-assistance",
  eligible = TRUE
)
recalled@roots[[1L]]@data

Saving a correction under the same ID creates a new immutable revision while leaving the original reference readable with graft_read().
